title: Shards of the Blighted March
models: OpenAI image generation through Codex's built-in image_gen tool
own_art_list: Original project-generated raster textures in game/textures/: forest-floor.webp, stone.webp, fir.webp, timber-detail.webp, plaster-detail.webp, meadow.webp, hornbeam-leaves.webp, oak-albedo.webp and limewash-albedo.webp.

Original project-generated ability illustrations in game/icons/: cleave.webp, slam.webp, cry.webp, firebolt.webp, frostnova.webp, blink.webp, shadowcut.webp, venom.webp, smoke.webp, forgeblow.webp, cinderbomb.webp and ironward.webp.
Original sound effects synthesized at runtime with the Web Audio API in game/src/audio.js; no prerecorded music or sound files.
In-game screenshots in screenshots/, captured from the running game.
what_i_found: I explored how much of a town-and-wilderness RPG can fit into a single browser tab: four classes, persistent loot, weapon upgrades and a complete four-region journey. Classes can be changed in settlements without resetting progress, making each return to town a chance to rethink the next hunt. Hills, rivers and bridges connect terrain, traversal, grounded attack warnings and a north-up atlas, so the landscape guides both exploration and combat; the procedural world also has potential for further visual improvements through richer models, textures and lighting.
